This Miscellaneous First Appeal Is Filed Under
Section 173(1) Of Mv Act Against The Judgment And Award
Dated 16.09.2016 Passed In Mvc No.9/2015 On The File Of
The Senior Civil Judge And Jmfc, Member Mact, K.R.Nagar,
Awrding Compensation Of Rs. 14,74,536/- With Interest At
9% P.A. From The Date Of Petition Till The Date Of Its
Realization.

This Miscellaneous First Appeal Coming On For
Hearing Through Physical Hearing/Video Conferencing,
This Day, The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

The present appeal is filed by the appellant - Karnataka State Road Transport Corporation (hereinafter for brevity referred to as 'KSRTC') under Section 173 (1) of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988, (hereinafter for brevity referred to as 'MV Act') against the judgment and award dated 16.09.2016 in M.V.C.No.9/2015 passed by the Senior Civil Judge & JMFC, Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, K.R. Nagar (hereinafter for brevity referred to as 'the Tribunal').
2.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, K.R. Nagar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The summary of the case of the claimant before the tribunal was that on the date 17.01.2015 at about 12.00 noon, deceased Syed Mohamed Haseebulla @ Haseeb @ Aseeb @ Aseefulla while going on a motorcycle as pillion rider and when they were near Cheeranahalli Circle, a KSRTC bus bearing registration No.KA-09-F-3568 being driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner dashed to the motorcycle.

entities.text: Syed Mohamed Haseebulla @ Haseeb @ Aseeb @ Aseefulla
entities.label: OTHER_PERSON

sentences.text: Due to the said road traffic accident, deceased fell down from the bike and sustained injuries.

He was shifted to Government Hospital at K.R. Nagar, from there to Apollo Hospital,
Mysuru, from there to K.R. Hospital, Mysuru and from there to JSS Hospital and again to K.R.
Hospital, Mysuru.
However, inspite of the treatment given the deceased died on the same day.
Claimant contended that she is the mother of the deceased and deceased was unmarried.
She contends that she was dependent on the deceased and that the deceased was doing tinkering and painting work and was earning `500/- to `600/- per day.
With this, she has claimed compensation of `18,65,000/- from the respondent showing it as owner cum insurer of the alleged offending bus.

3. In response to the notice, respondent before the tribunal appeared through its counsel and filed its statement of objection wherein, it has denied the occurrence of road traffic accident in the The Divisonal Controller vs Smt. Hasina Banu on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185869646/
2 manner as contended by the claimant.

entities.text: Divisonal Controller vs Smt. Hasina Banu
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It also denied that the deceased Syed Mohamed Haseebulla sustained injuries in the accident and succumbed to it.

The respondent further denied the age,
income and avocation of the deceased and the alleged dependency of the claimant on the deceased,
it denied its liability to pay the compensation.
4. Before the Tribunal, after framing the issues, the clamant has been examined as PW-1 and got examined one more witness as PW-2 and got marked documents from Exs.P.1 to P-9.

On behalf of KSRTC it got examined RW-1.
5.

After hearing from both sides, the Tribunal, by its impugned judgment dated 16.09.2016 allowed the claim petition in part, holding respondent (appellant herein) before it liable to pay the compensation to the claimant a sum of `14,74,536/- (after deducting `15,000/-) with interest thereupon at the rate of 9% per annum under the following heads with the sum shown against them:
 Sl. Compensation heads Compensation  No. amount in `
 1 Loss of dependency 14,14,536.00  2 Loss of love and affection 50,000.00  3 Funeral and obsequies 25,000.00  Total 14,89,536.00
6. Challenging the said judgment and award passed by the Tribunal, the appellant - has preferred this appeal.
7. The Trial Court records were called for and the same are placed before this Court.

9. Perused the materials placed before this Court including the memorandum of appeal, impugned judgment and also the Trial Court records.
10.
Heard the argument from the learned counsel for the appellant.

Inspite of granting sufficient opportunity, even as finally and making it clear that in case, if the arguments are not addressed on the next date of hearing, the Court may proceed to pass appropriate order, still, the learned counsel for the respondent neither appeared physically and nor through video conference and addressed his arguments.

As such, respondent's argument is taken as 'not addressed'.
11.

Learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant do not dispute the occurrence of the accident and finding of the tribunal on issue no.1 holding that the road traffic accident was occurred on the date and time as mentioned in the claim petition, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the KSRTC bus, however, the only contention of the appellant is about the quantum of compensation awarded by the tribunal under various heads and also the rate of interest awarded by The Divisonal Controller vs Smt. Hasina Banu on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185869646/
3

entities.text: Divisonal Controller vs Smt. Hasina Banu
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: the tribunal.
12. The occurrence of the road traffic accident on the date, time and place as alleged in the claim petition is reiterated by the claimant who got herself examined as PW-1.
The claimant got also examined one Sri. Shivarudrappa as PW- 2, who himself claims to be the eye witness to the alleged road traffic accident.

Their evidence is further corroborated by the documents which they have produced from Exs.P.1 to P.9 which interalia includes the copies of complaint to the police, FIR,
scene of offence panchanama, motor vehicle Inspector's report, postmortem report and the charge sheet.

The charge sheet at Ex.P.8 would go to show that the police after investigation have filed charge sheet against the driver of the KSRTC bus for the offences punishable under Sections 279,
337, 304A of IPC and Section 187 of the M.V. Act.

Thus, the evidence of PW-1 and PW-2 stands corroborated with the documentary evidence from Exs.P.1 to P.9 and go to establish that the road traffic accident on the date, time and place and in the manner as contended by the claimant has occurred, as such, the only point that remains for consideration is quantification of the compensation.
13.

Learned counsel for the appellant in his argument submitted that admittedly when the deceased was a bachelor and only dependant upon him is his mother, who is the claimant, the tribunal ought to have deducted 50% of the income towards personal expenses, whereas, it has deducted 1/3rd of his income towards personal expenses giving no reason for the same.
He further submitted that the quantum of compensation awarded towards love and affection, funeral and obsequies ceremonies are also on the higher side.
With this, he prayed for allowing the appeal.

14. As observed above, inspite of granting sufficient opportunities learned counsel for the respondent herein has remained absent, as such, it is taken that respondent has not addressed his arguments.

The appeal is of the year 2017 as such, six years old appeal which has arisen from a road traffic accident of the year 2015, hence, the Court by taking the argument of the learned counsel for the respondent as not addressed, proceeded further in hearing the appeal and disposing of the matter through this judgment.

15. The claimant contended that her deceased son at the time of death was doing the painting and tinkering work and was earning a sum of `500 to `600/- per day, however, except her oral statement no corroborating evidence has been produced by the claimant.

As such, the tribunal though has decided to take the notional income of the deceased for the relevant period however, in the said process it took a sum of `8,000/- per month as notional income of the deceased.

When in fact for the relevant year 2015, a large number of Motor Accident Claims Tribunals are being taking the notional income at `9,000/- per month, as such, the income of the deceased is required to be taken at `9,000/- per month.

Even according to the claimant the deceased was a bachelor and the claimant is said to be the mother of the deceased, as such there is only one claimant claiming herself - 10 - The Divisonal Controller vs Smt. Hasina Banu on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185869646/
4 dependent upon the deceased who was a bachelor.

entities.text: Divisonal Controller vs Smt. Hasina Banu on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the said circumstances, the tribunal was required to deduct 50% of his income towards his personal expenses.
However, without giving any reasons tribunal has taken deduction only at 1/3rd.
As such, if 50% deduction is made to the income of the deceased it comes to `4,500/- per month.

According to the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and others reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 since the deceased was self employed and as per the postmortem report and other police documents he was aged about 23 years at the time of road traffic accident, the future prospects is required to be added to the income of the deceased at 40% of the income.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and others reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, a sum of `1,800/- is to be added towards his contribution of `4,500/- to the claimant, which in total comes to a sum of `6,300/-.

The standard multiplier applicable for the age of the deceased is being '18' the quantum of compensation towards loss of dependency would be at `6,300/- x 12x 18 =
`13,60,800/-.

Towards conventional head as per Pranay Sethi's case (supra) a sum of `15,000/- towards funeral expenses, `15,000/- towards loss of estate and `40,000/- towards loss of consortium, thus a sum of `70,000/- is to be added.
18. Barring the above, the claimant/appellant is not entitled for compensation under any other heads or for enhancement of compensation under any other heads.

Thus, in total the appellant/claimant is entitled for the modified compensation as below:
 Compensation heads Compensation  amount in `
Loss of dependency 13,60,800.00  Loss of consortium 40,000.00
Funeral and obsequies 30,000.00  Total 14,30,800.00
19. The observation of the tribunal that interim compensation of a sum of `15,000/- has been paid by the respondent to the claimant immediately after the accident, is required to be deducted.

Thus, total compensation for which the claimant would be entitled is `14,30,800/- less `15,000/-
- 12 - = `14,15,800/-, since tribunal has awarded a sum of `14,74,536/- (after deduction of `15,000/-) the same is in excess of `58,736/-.
20.
Learned counsel for the appellant also contended that the tribunal has awarded an exorbitant rate of interest at 9% per annum.

Considering the fact that the fixed deposits in the Nationalised Banks are also not getting such a rate of interest for the relevant period, I am of the view that the The Divisonal Controller vs Smt. Hasina Banu on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185869646/
5 rate of interest is also required to be reduced confining it at 6% per annum.

entities.text: Divisonal Controller vs Smt. Hasina Banu on 21 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As such, the appeal deserves to be allowed in part.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal filed by KSRTC is allowed in part;
(ii) The quantum of compensation awarded by learned Senior Civil Judge & JMFC,
Member MACT, K.R. Nagar dated 16.09.2016 in M.V.C.No.9/2015 is hereby - 13 - modified and reduced to `14,15,800/-
(Rupees Fourteen Lakhs Fifteen Thousands Eight Hundred only).
(iii) The rate of interest awarded at 9% per annum in the impugned judgment and award also modified and reduced and fixed at 6% per annum on the awarded amount from the date of the petition till the date of realization.
(iv) The rest of the terms of the judgment and award of the Tribunal with respect to fixing the liability upon the respondent before the Tribunal and order regarding release of the amount shall all remains unaltered and unmodified.
- 14 - The amount deposited, if any, by the appellant in this appeal while filing the appeal be transmitted to the concerned tribunal by the registry without delay.
Draw the modified award accordingly.
Registry to transmit a copy of this judgment to the concerned Tribunal along with its records without delay.
Sd/-
